== (4) DESIGN DECISIONS ==

- Locking, not a narrow counter write. The brief offered a narrow 'increment this counter' path as a bonus ('removes the blast radius rather than serialising it'). Rejected: the directive counter lives inside _sys in the same file as every row, so a narrow write would require the exact raw string surgery that already produced the _standing skip-if-present defect and the _sync drop-cycle. Under a lock spanning read→write, the whole-file write is correct by construction (no writer can land between read and write, so nothing is reverted) and already has the T399 round-trip guard + T108 fsync + atomic tmp+rename. The rewrite cost (store is a few hundred KB) is negligible for a human-paced admin command. A genuinely narrow fix (derive directive ids from the append-only ledger instead of a store counter) is a candidate follow-up, not this task.
- Migration lock placement: taken on EVERY invocation, read-only verbs included, because the decision to write depends on the read; a pre-read outside the lock would reopen the window. The lock is held only for read+parse+(maybe)write.
- cmdTell verify-after-write: directiveIsReadable() re-reads the ledger under the same lock and fails loudly ('FATAL: directive D0NN is NOT readable back from the ledger...') — the silent-success tell is what hid the incident.
- registerStanding's writes became writeStateLocked (the caller holds the flock; writeState would re-flock a second fd and self-deadlock per BSD flock semantics). persistStandingState is documented as safe only under the caller's lock.

== (5) SIBLING DEFECT (OUT OF SCOPE, reported) ==

serializeState emits tasks + _sys only; parseStateJson skips `_`-prefixed keys. So _standing and _sync are raw passthrough keys: any writeStateLocked from another command silently erases them until the next standing/sync run rewrites them. Effect: the standing trigger priors (c3_prior, msg_prior, false_prior, dirty_prior) read 0 after any other store write, so the growth-triggers (X > prior and prior > 0) cannot fire across a store write by another command. persistStandingState's 'skip if already present' path is therefore reached only when _standing was just dropped. Real fix: make _standing (and _sync) first-class fields of StateMap in parse/serialize/free.

== (6) T544 LINKAGE ==

Arm 2 demonstrates the exact mechanism by which a concurrent unlocked writer reverts a claim's field writes. A `done` that recorded model/verdict into the store can be reverted by a later unlocked whole-file write (tell/migration/standing/sync/assert). This is a CANDIDATE cause for T544's 152 of 193 null-model rows — mechanism established with a reproduction, NOT proven against the historical store (that needs T544's own forensics on the archived rows and commit timeline). The T545 control script's arm 2 is directly reusable by T544.
